segments.english: From the time the government opened the school, the children were studying Scripture and its translations, Onkelos and Rabbi Saadia Gaon, Mishnah and the Rambam, and grammar and the explanation of the words, All was done properly the study of the Torah, Prophets and Writings with clear explanation, a grammar book of the Holy Tongue! and the study of the Turkish language through the Turkish teacher, upright of heart, Chafetz Effendi. And after him Zia Bey with wonderful diligence! and we accustomed them to speak one with another in Hebrew and in Turkish, so that they would be well accustomed in their mouths, And at the turn of the year the examiners came from the government, may his majesty be exalted, and the children arranged their studies in Turkish and they showed them their writing, and the examiners saw their talents shining in their studies, and they praised them, that they are educated! Also the Hebrew examiners came on the day after and the children arranged their studies before them in Hebrew and in Arabic, and they found favour in their eyes for the ability of their studies, and praised them! And the following year the children did so, studying with diligence and alacrity, And at the end of the year the Turkish examiners came and examined them with uprightness of heart, and praised them, that they were making progress in their studies, and urged them with words and blessed them! But the Hebrew examiners who came after them had already begun to flare up among them the hatred of enlightenment and the study of languages. And they began to provoke them and to ask them about what they had not yet studied, and whoever could not answer anything anywhere they asked him, by the standard due to a complete sage, was counted by them as nothing at all. In order to diminish their honour, to sadden them and to slacken their hands from the studies, and they sought faults and blemishes in each and every one, and out of malice they did not turn to the studies and the knowledge that the children had acquired. Only to trip them up over what they had not yet studied, and to question them on the order of Nezikin, while they were still at the order of Moed, and when they showed them the beauty of their writing, the splendid and orderly Ashuri script, they sought a fault in the joining, as fine as a hair's thread, in some of the letters, as if they were writing S-T-V-M. And they did not look at the beauty of the script and its order. And in the interpretation of the Writings they asked them to solve difficult verses, such as "Binding his foal to the vine", and the like, and they went out from before them in low spirits, good, grieved, sad and with limp hands.

tokens.note: אשר is a relative here: 'when' (the time at which the government opened the school).
את before a definite object has no English word.
בית הספר: 'house of the book', the word for school; the English gives 'the school'.
ורס״ג: Rabbi Saadia Gaon (רב סעדיה גאון), the abbreviation expanded as the decisions require.
הרמב״ם: the Rambam, Maimonides.
ופי׳ is ופירוש, 'explanation'.
בפי׳ is בפירוש, 'with explanation'.
לשון הקדש: the Hebrew language, 'the holy tongue'.
התורקית: Turkish, the language of the government.
The name is given as the text spells it (חאפץ), in the project's scheme as Chafetz; no identification is made.
אפנדי: the Turkish title Effendi.
זיא: the name as the text spells it; no identification is made.
ביי: the Turkish title Bey.
הרגלנום: a hif'il perfect, first person plural, with the object suffix ם: 'we accustomed them'.
יר״ה: the honorific of the government, rendered as the decisions give it.
משכילים: 'educated' here; the same word is the name the Haskalah gave its adherents, and the English does not settle that sense.
הבוחנים העברים: the Hebrew examiners; the text does not say who appointed them.
התורקים: the Turks, the examiners of the government.
חיל: literally 'strength'; in עושים חיל בלימודים it means 'making progress in the studies'.
ההשכלה: enlightenment, the movement called the Haskalah.
לקנתרם: to provoke, to vex.
The witness spells הלמודים; it is read as הלימודים (see apparatus).
לקפחם: to put them down, to trip them up; literally 'to diminish them'.
נזיקים: Nezikin, the order of the Mishnah on damages.
מועד: Moed, the order of the Mishnah on festivals.
כתב אשורי: the Ashuri script, the square Hebrew letters.
דיבוק: the joining of letters; the fault sought is in the joining.
סתו״מ is an abbreviation not expanded in decisions.md; it is kept as its letters, and its expansion is open.
אסרי לגפן עירה: Gen 49:11, quoted.

grammar: The paragraph is a chain of clauses joined by ו and by the time phrases that open each school year: ולתקופת השנה (3:63), ולשנה האחרת (3:111), ובצאת השנה (3:119). The sentence that begins with ומעת has its main verb in היו הילדים לומדים (3:8).
והרגלנום לדבר זה עם זה (3:50) is a hif'il perfect with an object suffix; the purpose clause כדי שיהיו מורגלים בפיהם היטב (3:58) follows it.
The sentence ואחריו זיא ביי בחריצות נפלאה! (3:45-3:49) has no verb, and the English adds none beyond the words.

The turn to hostility comes at אך (3:139): the Hebrew examiners who came after them are set against the Turkish examiners, and the verb התחילה (3:145) starts the change. The purpose clause כדי להפחית כבודם (3:176) states the aim.
The phrase אסרי לגפן עירה (3:248-3:250) is quoted as an example of a hard verse, so the English keeps quotation marks; the source is Gen 49:11.
segments.note: Translated from the Wikisource witness as base text. The paragraph is ironic in the author's framing: the examiners first praise the children, then the Hebrew examiners set out to shame them. משכילים and ההשכלה are rendered in neutral terms; see the token notes.
apparatus: Witness spelling הלמודים (1:3.195) is read as the evident word הלימודים.
Bible verse: Gen 49:11, 'Binding his foal to the vine' (אסרי לגפן עירה), quoted as an example of a hard verse (1:3.248-1:3.250).
The abbreviation סתו״מ (1:3.233) is not expanded in decisions.md; it is kept as the letters S-T-V-M.
Base text: the Wikisource witness, not yet collated against the 1931 scan (open question 2).
context: The government (הממשלה), its examiners, its teacher and its language are called Turkish (התורקים, התורקית). The text names no place and no date for the school.
